title: I built a multiplayer stock market sim with Claude, where fundamentals, interest rates and news move prices
author: Squeeekr
selftext:
I'm an economics student with no coding background, and I built a multiplayer stock market game with Claude Code.

**What it is:** a live market where companies have real cash, debt and earnings, interest rates move valuations, and news hits prices. You trade against other players, take bank loans, and compete on the standings. You can play as a guest, with no signup.

**How AI was used:**

* Claude Code wrote all the code, mostly Opus 5.5 on high. I switched to Sonnet for mechanics questions and brainstorming to save tokens.
* I had it run simulations to balance the stocks and market behavior, which let me tune parameters without guessing. This was the most useful part.
* The video was also made with Opus 5.5. The quality surprised me, though it's a bit generic.

Curious what you'd add or change. Any feedback on the game or the workflow is welcome 😄

comments.author: ClashAtNightfall
comments.body:
Think the simulated run needs a color gradient based on success or failure so a 0-15% = colorAshadeA, 16-30% AB 31-49 AC etc. it's just too illegible at a glance to see top performers etc

Interesting concept though. Now I can lose fake money instead of real money 👍

replies.author: Squeeekr
replies.body:
Definitely if I was going to present it! (which I guess I did now lol). This one was just to fix the sharpe ratio a bit, as the volatile stocks were way too OP in the early simulations.

You should give it a try! Most of us are losing money so getting to the top isn't hard 😅
